sentences.text: The present Writ Petition is filed questioning action of the Respondents 3 and 4 in interfering with the business of the Petitioners and closing down some of the flavoured water units on the basis of the cyclostyled notices issued in the last week of February-2016 by Respondent No.4 on behalf of Respondent No.3 as illegal and arbitrary.

2. Learned counsel for the Petitioners would submit that the Petitioners have established flavoured water units and carrying business by complying the relevant provisions as per law applicable, after registering under A.P.Shops and Establishments Act, 1988.

3. While so, notices were issued to the Petitioners, wherein the Petitioners were directed to do business after obtaining permission from the Bureau of Indian Standards (in short 'BIS') Certificate of permission from the R.D.O, Guntur and other statutory permissions.

4. Learned counsel for the Petitioners would contend that there is no requirement to obtain BIS Certificate or permission from any other Authority, on the ground that there is no standard as prescribed by the BIS and therefore, no BIS Certificate is required and only requirement is from Food Safety Standards of India (in short 'FSSAI').

It is also further contended that there is no power to the Commissioner or Health Officer to insist the Petitioners to get permissions under separate enactments i.e R.D.O/ Tahsildar under WALTA Act and it is for the Authority concerned to take action, if there is any requirement to get permission in the matter.
5.

The Respondent No.3 filed Counter-Affidavit, wherein it is stated that pursuant to the interim order, this Court, the possession of the closed units were restored to the Petitioners and that Respondent No.3 would not interfere to the operations of the Petitioners, except in accordance with law.

6. Considering the arguments of the learned counsel for the Petitioners and in the light of Counter-Affidavit filed by the Respondent No.3, the interim order passed in similar set of cases, the Respondents are directed not to interfere with the business activities of the Petitioner without following procedure as laid down under law.
7. With the above direction, the present Writ Petition, is therefore, disposed of.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
